_note: Explicitness ladder for the CDIM dose-response experiment. L0 = the six-line abstract substrate of 17 Sep 2026 (retired from prompts/ on 19 Sep, kept here as ladder/L0.txt; the first-round results were measured on it); L1-L5 are templates with the same six bullet slots, each doing one more step of the inference chain for the model. S = the official prompts/substrate.txt (nine lines, Definitions block, read live, never edited here); pro = the retired substrate_pro.txt (ladder/pro.txt). Templated levels are filled per scenario by build_prompts.py with the scenario fields plus the object-class phrases below; the others are used verbatim. 'features' are objective explicitness markers per level. 'order' is the x-axis of the dose-response figure.

L0.step: abstract: object / location A / location B / activity / vehicle / operate

L1.step: L0 + the answer verbs named where the rule bears on them (walks / drives / drive it)

L2.step: L1 + concrete nouns as parenthetical examples (for example a car / the car wash / home)

L3.step: concrete nouns replace every abstraction (the car, home, the car wash, wash the car)

L4.step: L3 + every line states its consequence for the walk/drive decision

L5.step: L4 + line 6 states the verdict (the correct answer is drive, not walk)

S.step: the official substrate: abstract rules plus a Definitions block that names object = car, service location = car wash; consequences of walking stated (leaves a vehicle behind), no verdict

pro.step: retired substrate_pro: definitions with alternatives (car, book; car wash, library, gas station), consequences stated, no verdict

vehicle.move_clause: walking moves only the user, driving moves both
vehicle.line5_L4: If the user walks to the {place}, the {object} stays at {origin} and the user cannot {task3}; walking fails.
vehicle.line6_L4: A {object} is a vehicle: the user must drive the {object} to bring it to the {place}; driving succeeds.
vehicle.line6_L5: A {object} is a vehicle: the user must drive the {object} to the {place}. The correct answer is drive, not walk.

portable.move_clause: the user can carry it while walking
portable.line5_L4: If the user walks to the {place} carrying the {object}, the {object} arrives and the user can {task3}; walking works.
portable.line6_L4: A {object} is a portable item: the user can carry the {object} to the {place} on foot; walking succeeds.
portable.line6_L5: A {object} is a portable item: the user can carry the {object} to the {place} on foot. The correct answer is walk, not drive.
